# ADR-015: One daemon decides, nodes on owner devices execute

- **Status:** Proposed
- **Date:** 2026-11-09

## Decision
Jaari runs anywhere by splitting brain from hands. One daemon (`apps/daemon`) is the control plane: sessions, memory, gate, scheduler, channels, LLM routing, and the notification ledger. It runs where the owner puts it (laptop, home server, VPS). Effectful hands run on **nodes** (`apps/node`): a thin executor on any owner device that enrols with a `device` identity (the same pairing as channels, OQ-02), advertises capabilities (`browser.local` on the pinned profile of ADR-005, `desktop.macos`, `desktop.linux`, `files`, `shell`), executes only actions the gate has already approved, and streams results and screenshots back. A single-machine install runs a node inside the daemon process; Docker and Firecracker backends are nodes too. Nodes talk to the daemon over a mutually authenticated connection on the owner's overlay network (Tailscale, Headscale, or plain WireGuard) or the daemon's own WebSocket; a node holds no memory, no LLM credentials, and no secrets beyond its device key. `secretRef` values are resolved by the daemon's executor and sent to the node just in time for one action, which fills them into the page and discards them (ADR-007). Takeover (ADR-005) and the live view (OQ-34) are node features because the node is the only place the owner's screen exists. An offline node queues approved actions with an expiry and the owner is told once; capabilities a node does not advertise are not offered to the model. Where the daemon runs decides the egress identity of `web.fetch`; where the node runs decides the egress identity of `browser.*` (OQ-32).

## Alternatives rejected
One process on one machine (a VPS daemon cannot reach the owner's browser profile; a laptop daemon is asleep half the day); a cloud VM per owner by default (the Instinct, Muse, and Grok Bot shape: datacenter IP, credentials off-device); several full daemons (split brain for memory, approvals, and budgets); nodes with their own LLM access (unauditable, secrets sprawl); nodes that resolve `secretRef` themselves (every device becomes a vault client).
